'''John Edward Morton''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|QSO|FRSNZ}} {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FLS}} (18 July 1923 – 6 March 2011) was a [[biologist]], philosopher, [[theologian]], and [[conservation movement|conservationist]] from New Zealand. 

Morton is regarded as one of New Zealand's most respected scientists,<ref name=":0">{{cite news |date=8 March 2011 |title=John Morton obituary |url=https://notices.nzherald.co.nz/nz/obituaries/nzherald-nz/name/john-morton-obituary?pid=149120606 |access-date=23 April 2022 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Obituary: John Morton B.Sc., M.Sc. (Auckland), Ph.D., D.Sc. (London), FRSNZ, QSO (18 July 1923–6 March 2011) |url=https://www.mapress.com/mr/content/v31/2011f/n2p140.htm |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=www.mapress.com}}</ref> and one of New Zealand's greatest marine biologists, researching New Zealand's [[ecology]] and [[marine life]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Mackie |first1=Andrew S. Y. |last2=Dales |first2=Clare |last3=Kent |first3=R. Michael L. |last4=Dixon |first4=David R. |last5=Wells |first5=Rufus M. G. |last6=Warren |first6=Lynda M. |date=2020-12-28 |title=Rodney Phillips Dales: influential annelid researcher, natural historian, editor, artist, gardener and architectural enthusiast (1927–2020) |url=https://www.mapress.com/zs/article/view/zoosymposia.19.1.5 |journal=Zoosymposia |language=en |volume=19 |pages=10–26 |doi=10.11646/zoosymposia.19.1.5 |issn=1178-9913}}</ref>

He was the first chair of the School of Zoology and Biological Sciences at the [[University of Auckland]], a position he held for 28 years from 1959 to 1988; and published more than one hundred scientific papers and theological works in a career of over 50 years of scientific research.

He was deeply interested in the much wider fields of natural history and philosophy; was a noted theologian; and political and conservation activist.

He authored numerous books, papers, and newspaper columns across a wide variety of topics; and was also the presenter of the imported nature and science television programme, ''Our World''.<ref name="herald">{{cite news |title=Obituary: Professor John Edward Morton |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/education/news/article.cfm?c_id=35&objectid=10711761 |last=Pickmere |first=Arnold |newspaper=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=12 March 2011 |accessdate=26 September 2011}}</ref>

==Early life==
Morton was born in [[Morrinsville]] in 1923. His family used to holiday at [[Milford, New Zealand|Milford Beach]], where began his lifelong interest in the seashore and natural history. He attended [[Morrinsville College]], completing high school as [[Dux#Education|dux]] in 1940.<ref>{{Cite news |date=4 May 2011 |title=Eminent scientist greatly admired |url= |work=Piako Post  |pages=8}}</ref>

==Career==

=== Biologist ===
Morton enrolled at [[University of Auckland|Auckland University College]] in 1942, shortly before his eighteenth birthday, and graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in zoology in 1945.

He continued at Auckland University researching a range of molluscan taxa until he moved to the United Kingdom in 1950 under a Dominian and Colonial Scholarship to undertake doctoral research at the [[University of London]] under the supervision of [[Alastair Graham]], working from Plymouth on the evolution of marine pulmonates of the family Ellobiidae. He remained at the university of London lecturing and studying molluscs until 1959.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last1=Gordon |first1=Dennis P |last2=and Ballantine |first2=Bill |date=2013-09-01 |title=Contribution of the Leigh Marine Laboratory to knowledge of marine species diversity |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00288330.2013.810159 |journal=New Zealand Journal of Marine and Freshwater Research |volume=47 |issue=3 |pages=277–293 |doi=10.1080/00288330.2013.810159 |bibcode=2013NZJMF..47..277G |issn=0028-8330|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=John Edward Morton {{!}} Shellers From the Past and Present |url=https://www.conchology.be/?t=9001&id=25433&srsltid=AfmBOoqE6vPqrZJZbVIGzMS5TWlEOY8dbmZ0V4v6it9L3yGpN48QXIda |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=www.conchology.be |language=en}}</ref>

This period was the most productive decade of his working life as a biologist in terms of the volume of his output, during which he published 33 papers (31 of them sole-authored) and his first book, ''Molluscs'' (1958),<ref name=":2" />  which stayed in print for over 20 years over nine editions.<ref name=":1" />

The 1950s established his international reputation in malacology.<ref name=":4" />

Morton returned to New Zealand in 1960,<ref>[https://nzsc.wordpress.com/1960-1969/1960-8th-april-rangitiki/ Free online Passenger Listing for the April 1960 voyage of the New Zealand Shipping Company's ''Rangitiki'' on which the Morton family travelled from London to New Zealand.]</ref> having been appointed the first chair of the School of Zoology and Biological Sciences at the [[University of Auckland]], a position he held for 28 years from 1959 to 1988.<ref name="herald" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name="Anglican_Taonga">{{cite news |date=6 March 2011 |title=Professor John Morton dies |url=http://anglicantaonga.org.nz/News/TIKANGA-PAKEHA/Creation-theologian-dies |accessdate=26 September 2011 |newspaper=Anglican Taonga}}</ref> The then vice-chancellor, Kenneth Maidment, said “'Morton, we’ve brought you here to build up a good zoology department—world standard. Don’t worry about the money—we’ll see you get what you need.'”<ref name=":1" />

In the early 1960s, Morton, with [[Val Chapman]], was instrumental in founding the [[Leigh Marine Laboratory|Leigh Marine Biology Laboratory]], which opened in 1964.<ref name=":4" /> 

In 1965, at the request of the [[Royal Society]], Morton lead the marine party of the [[Royal Society Expedition to the British Solomon Islands Protectorate|Royal Society’s Expedition to the British Solomon Islands.]]<ref name="Whos who">{{cite book |title=Who's Who in New Zealand |publisher=Reed |year=1978 |isbn=0-589-01113-8 |editor-last=Traue |editor-first=J. E. |editor-link=Jim Traue |edition=11th |location=Wellington |page=201}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

In 1968 Morton and Michael Miller published ''The New Zealand Sea Shore'', an authoritative “classic” work on New Zealand’s littoral zone.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Williams |first=G. R. |date=1969 |title=Review of The New Zealand sea shore |url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/24061373 |journal=Proceedings (New Zealand Ecological Society) |issue=16 |pages=83 |jstor=24061373 |issn=0077-9946}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=John Morton was one of a kind |url=https://www.nzgeo.com/stories/john-morton-was-one-of-a-kind/ |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=New Zealand Geographic |language=en-NZ}}</ref> It is considered the foundation on which all New Zealand’s marine biology has been built, with Professor Bill Ballantine describing it as, “It is still the best single book on seashores in the world.”<ref name=":1" />

Morton’s continuing interest in the Pacific lead to substantial research in Fiji, Samoa, Cook Islands, New Caledonia and Papua New Guinea. 

In 1974 he was Royal Society Visiting Professor in Zoology in Hong Kong, which led to the production in 1983, with Professor Brian Morton, of ''The Sea Shore Ecology of Hong Kong.''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tjepkema |first=John D. |date=21 July 1983 |title=Postgate's fixation |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/304284a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=304 |issue=5923 |pages=284 |doi=10.1038/304284a0 |bibcode=1983Natur.304..284T |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Morton |first1=John |title=The sea shore ecology of Hong Kong |last2=Morton |first2=Brian |date=1983 |publisher=Hong Kong Univ. Pr |isbn=978-962-209-027-9 |location=Hong Kong}}</ref>

In 1977 he was appointed visiting professor at St Andrew’s University, New Brunswick, Canada and taught and researched at Vancouver Island, and on the Atlantic shores of Canada.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" />

He was considered at this time one of New Zealand's most talented up-and-coming academics,<ref name="Mike Lee">{{cite web |url=http://www.mikelee.co.nz/2011/03/tribute-to-a-great-new-zealander-farewell-prof-john-morton/ |title=Tribute to a great New Zealander – farewell Prof John Morton |last=Lee |first=Mike |date=14 March 2011 |accessdate=26 September 2011}}</ref> and was later regarded by many as one of New Zealand's greatest marine biologists.<ref name="Anglican_Taonga" /><ref name=":1">{{cite news |title=John Morton |journal=[[New Zealand Geographic]] |url=http://www.nzgeographic.co.nz/issue-69/john-morton |issue=69 |date=Sep–Oct 2004 |accessdate=26 September 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402233016/http://www.nzgeographic.co.nz/issue-69/john-morton |archivedate=2 April 2012 }}</ref>

His teaching style and influence have been well-documented in ''A History of Biology at Auckland University 1883–1983''.<ref>{{Citation |title=A History of Biology at Auckland University 1883–1983 |type=Research Report |publisher=Department of Biology, University of Auckland |year=1983 |first1=Brian |last1=Foster |first2=Jack |last2=Rattenbury |first3=John |last3=Marbrook}}</ref> He believed in "humanising" complex scientific issues, and presenting them in laymen's language.<ref name="herald" />

In 2004 he published ''Seashore ecology of New Zealand and the Pacific'',<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Morton |first1=John Edward |title=Seashore ecology of New Zealand and the Pacific |last2=Hayward |first2=Bruce W. |date=2004 |publisher=Bateman |isbn=978-1-86953-399-1 |location=Auckland, N.Z}}</ref> the culmination of his life’s work as a biologist.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Auckland Museum Institute Conchology Section Newsletter |url=https://www.aucklandshellclub.net.nz/mar2005.htm |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=www.aucklandshellclub.net.nz}}</ref>

=== Theologian ===
Morton was regarded as one of New Zealand's leading Christian academics. He was Lay Canon of Holy Trinity Cathedral, Auckland; Fellow St. John’s Theological College, Auckland and sat for more than 20 years on the General Synod of the New Zealand Anglican Church.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Anjali |date=2011-10-03 |title=God's Scientist: John Morton Archive |url=https://www.kinderlibrary.ac.nz/gods-scientist-john-morton/ |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=John Kinder Theological Library |language=en-NZ}}</ref> At his funeral eulogy, Bishop John Paterson told mourners that Morton’s knowledge of theology was highly respected in the Anglican Church.<ref name="Mike Lee" />

Morton believed in a unified view of [[science and religion]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=183940 |title=Let's thank God for the wonder that is science |last=Watkin |first=Tim |newspaper=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=21 April 2001 |accessdate=26 September 2011}}</ref> He told ''[[The New Zealand Herald]]'' upon his retirement in 1988 that "I find that my scientific work has confirmed my Christian convictions. To me biology and [[theology]] complement each other."<ref name="herald" /> 

In his 1984 book ''Redeeming Creation''<ref>{{Cite book |title=Redeeming Creation |publisher=[[Zealandia (newspaper)|Zealandia]] |year=1984 |location=Auckland}}</ref> he acknowledged the influence of the French [[palaeontologist]] [[Teilhard de Chardin]] in forming the [[teleological]] view he expounded in his academic life.

Morton’s theological works include ''Man, Science and God'' (1972); ''Redeeming Creation'' (1984); and ''Christ, Creation and the Environment'' (1989).

=== Conservationist ===
Morton did much for conservation in New Zealand. In 1975, he was a leader in the establishment of New Zealand's first [[marine reserve]], [[Cape Rodney-Okakari Point Marine Reserve]] (which is near Cape Rodney and [[Leigh, New Zealand|Leigh]] and includes [[Te Hāwere-a-Maki / Goat Island]]).<ref name="herald"/> He led the conservation movement to a series of victories in the 1970s and 1980s, which saved the last of New Zealand's mainland native forests, [[Pureora Forest Park|Pureora]], [[Whirinaki Forest Park|Whirinaki]], [[Waitututu]] and [[South Westland]] from [[logging]].<ref name="Mike Lee"/>

In 1980, for his conservation work, he was made a Companion in New Zealand’s Queen’s Service Order.<ref name=":2" /> 

In 2000 he was awarded the Biodiversity Accolade from the Minister of Conservation for his outstanding and sustained contributions towards conserving New Zealand’s unique plants and animals and the places where they live.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Sandra |title=Biodiversity Accolades announced |url=https://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/biodiversity-accolades-announced |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=www.beehive.govt.nz}}</ref>

Notable conservation works include ''Seacoast in the Seventies - The Future of the New Zealand Shoreline'' (1973) and ''The future of New Zealand conservation: Ethics and Politics'' (1995)''.''

=== Politician ===
Morton served on the [[Auckland Regional Authority]] from 1971 to 1974 for [[Takapuna]], losing his re-election bid after switching his party affiliation to [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Auckland's eco warriors come in many guises |author=John Roughan |newspaper=The New Zealand Herald |date=12 March 2011 |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10711778}}</ref> In 1989 he became a founding member of the [[NewLabour Party (New Zealand)|New Labour Party]], which in 1991 formed a coalition with other parties called the [[Alliance (New Zealand political party)|Alliance]].<ref name="Mike Lee" />

* [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] (1969)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-fellows/m-o/ |title=List of all Fellows with surnames M–O |publisher=Royal Society Te Apārangi |accessdate=31 August 2020}}</ref>

Literary awards, 1950s onwards |url=https://teara.govt.nz/en/awards-and-prizes/page-2 |website=Te Ara – The Encyclopedia of New Zealand |access-date=27 February 2021}}</ref>

*Chairman, Forest and Bird Protection Society

== Influence and Legacy ==
[[Bill Ballantine (biologist)|Bill Ballantine]] said of Morton: “There are not too many shore ecologists who have saved forests, significantly advanced the cause of women’s equality, articulated considered positions on the centrality of God in the cosmos and on free public transport, and who can write speeches in Latin.”<ref name=":1" />

Morton is honoured by the NZ Marine Sciences Society’s Professor John Morton Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=JOHN MORTON MEDAL |url=https://nzmss.org/awards/john-morton-medal/ |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=New Zealand Marine Sciences Society |language=en-US}}</ref>

Morton had a significant influence on many people across wide fields including:

* Professor [[Bill Ballantine (biologist)|Bill Ballantine]], Morton’s first PhD student and winner of the 1996 [[Goldman Environmental Prize]] for his promotion of marine reserves.<ref name=":1" /> 
* Dame [[Patricia Bergquist]], the first person to earn a doctoral degree in zoology from the University of Auckland, and whose PhD Morton supervised. Bergquist later became Professor of Zoology at Auckland University.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Bergquist |first=Patricia |title=The Demospongiae of New Zealand-Systematics, distribution and relationships |type=Doctoral thesis |publisher=ResearchSpace@Auckland, University of Auckland |url=https://researchspace.auckland.ac.nz/handle/2292/2189 |year=1961 |hdl=2292/2189}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Patricia Rose Bergquist |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/obituaries/fellows-obituaries/patricia-rose-bergquist |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref>
* [[John Croxall]], who completed a PhD at the [[University of Auckland]] in 1971, on [[Ascidiacea|ascidian]] ecology, supervised by Morton, who went on to be Head of Conservation Biology at the [[British Antarctic Survey]].<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Croxall |first=John |title=Digestive system, feeding and ecology of some New Zealand intertidal ascidians |type=Doctoral thesis |publisher=ResearchSpace@Auckland, University of Auckland |year=1971 |hdl=2292/772}}</ref>
* Dr Rodney Phillips Dales, who met Morton at [[Queen Mary University of London|Queen Mary College]], and became life-long friends with Morton.<ref name=":3" />
* Brian Arthur Foster, Associate Professor of Zoology.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Buckeridge |first1=John S. |last2=Newman |first2=William A. |date=1994 |title=Brian Arthur Foster, 10 July, 1942-26 June, 1992 |url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/20104944 |journal=Crustaceana |volume=66 |issue=2 |pages=247–252 |doi=10.1163/156854094X00738 |jstor=20104944 |issn=0011-216X}}</ref>
* Dr Dennis Preston Gordon, former student, and senior scientist at the [[National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Smith |first1=Abigail |last2=Bock |first2=Philip |last3=Batson |first3=Peter |date=2016 |title=The contribution of Dennis P. Gordon to the understanding of New Zealand Bryozoa |url=https://ojs.victoria.ac.nz/nzsr/article/view/8528/7583 |journal=New Zealand Science Review |language=en |volume=73 |issue=3–4 |pages=67–71 |doi=10.26686/nzsr.v73i3-4.8528 |issn=2624-277X|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* [[Jeremy Griffith]], Australian biologist, whose work Morton compared to that of Teilhard de Chardin, launching one of Griffith’s books in New Zealand in 1992, and commending his 2003 book ''A Species In Denial'' as “superb”.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Emeritus Professor John Morton – Reviews and Feedback |url=https://www.humancondition.com/prof-john-morton/ |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=World Transformation Movement |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Griffith |first=Jeremy |title=A Species In Denial |year=2004 |isbn=978-1741290011}}</ref>
* Professor John C. Montgomery, Institute of Marine Science, University of Auckland, for whom Morton sparked “a purpose and goal”.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Montgomery |first=John C |date=2022-07-01 |title=What will the future make of our discoveries? |url=https://academic.oup.com/icesjms/article/79/5/1435/6585090 |journal=ICES Journal of Marine Science |volume=79 |issue=5 |pages=1435–1444 |doi=10.1093/icesjms/fsac080 |issn=1054-3139|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Kennedy P. Warne, former student, founding editor of [[New Zealand Geographic]].<ref name=":1" />
